columns.rationale: Two-letter IATA carrier code with null_rate 0.0 and distinct_count 16 over 16 rows, so every value is unique and populated (distinct_values include '9E', 'AA', 'WN', 'YV').
Full carrier name with null_rate 0.0 and distinct_count 16, one label per carrier (for example 'Delta Air Lines Inc.' and 'Virgin America'); kept as free text since values are proper names.
Flagged is_airbyte_metadata: true; a capture-tool surrogate id (distinct_count 16, one UUID per landed row) with no business meaning.
Flagged is_airbyte_metadata: true; a single extraction timestamp (distinct_count 1, min = max = '2026-09-02T23:26:17') describing the load, not the airline.
Flagged is_airbyte_metadata: true; constant empty JSON payload (distinct_count 1, distinct_values ['{}']) emitted by the capture tool.

decisions.rationale: dataset.duplicate_row_rate is 0.0 across dataset.row_count 16, so no exact duplicate rows exist in bronze and no dedupe step is proposed.

carrier has distinct_count 16 over row_count 16 with null_rate 0.0, so one row per carrier code; name is equally unique but a code is the stabler key, and a human should confirm uniqueness against the warehouse.

_airbyte_raw_id, _airbyte_extracted_at, and _airbyte_meta all carry is_airbyte_metadata: true and describe the Airbyte load (constant timestamp, constant '{}' payload, per-row UUID) rather than the airline.
Both business columns landed as VARCHAR and their distinct_values are short alphabetic codes and proper names, so no numeric or temporal cast is supported by the evidence.
carrier and name each report null_count 0 and null_rate 0.0, so both are proposed required with null_handling not_applicable.

purpose: silver_airlines is the cleaned carrier reference table derived from bronze.nyc_airlines: one row per two-letter IATA carrier code with its full airline name, intended as a lookup dimension for flight fact tables.
usage: Join on carrier to decode a flight's two-letter code into a display name; the table is tiny (16 rows) and intended for broadcast-style joins. Treat name as a display label only, since it is free-form text and may be restated by the source.
limitations: The table carries only the two business columns present in bronze; all Airbyte capture columns were dropped, so no load timestamp or lineage id survives into silver. Uniqueness of carrier is asserted from a 16-row snapshot where distinct_count equals row_count and duplicate_row_rate is 0.0, so it must be re-measured if the source grows or begins carrying historical carrier records.
